script: You say one word to your dog and their head snaps sideways like you just asked them the meaning of life. It's one of the most adorable things dogs do, and scientists actually have a few solid theories about why. The first is about hearing. Dogs have much better hearing range than we do, and tilting their head helps them pinpoint exactly where a sound is coming from, kind of like adjusting a satellite dish. The second theory is about seeing your face. Dogs' muzzles can block part of their view, so tilting their head shifts their eyes just enough to actually see your mouth and expression while you're talking. And here's the part dog owners love. Some researchers believe dogs tilt their heads more often when they hear words they actually recognize, like their name or the word walk. It's their brain working extra hard to connect the sound to something meaningful. So that head tilt isn't just cute. It's your dog literally trying harder to understand you, using their ears, their eyes, and their memory all at once. Which honestly says a lot about how much they actually care about what you're saying.
